newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-HK tax reform may be needed, banker says.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-HK tax reform may be needed, banker says.

text.p: A leading Hong Kong banker, Hang Seng Bank Ltd chief executive Alexander Au, said on Thursday tax relief may need to be given to the territory's fund managers for them to keep pace with regional competitors.

Such a measure is likely to be recommended soon by a Hong Kong Trade Development Council advisory committee set up to find ways of protecting and elevating Hong Kong's role as a financial services hub, Au said.
"We are aware of the favourable treatment by Singapore to certain sectors of the service industry," Au told a business forum in Melbourne.
"We may have to match Singapore in some areas and so the recommendations will probably be forthcoming in a couple of weeks or months and we hope actions will spring from that."
Later, Au told Reuters he was referring to relative tax rates on company profits in Hong Kong and Singapore.
Hong Kong-based fund managers are subject, like all of the territory's companies, to a flat tax rate of 16.5 percent while Singapore-based fund managers only pay 10 percent, he said.
"That is my personal view," he said.
"I don't think I should pre-empt the (review)."
